sample_unit: orthopedic procedure notes with surgeon-labeled benchmark CPT codes

links.outcome: Run-to-run consistency of LLM CPT code outputs across three repeated queries
links.effect: Gemini had highest consistency (72.7% identical outputs across runs); Claude 63.6%; complex multi-component procedures showed greater inter-run variance.
links.quote: Consistency did not correlate with accuracy: Gemini demonstrated the highest run-to-run consistency (72.7% identical outputs across runs) despite lower benchmark alignment, while Claude showed greater variance (63.6%) yet superior accuracy.

links.outcome: LLM CPT code accuracy against surgeon-labeled ground-truth reference standard
links.effect: Claude Opus 4.5 F1 65.9% (precision 66.7%, recall 65.2%); Gemini 3 Pro F1 62.1%; GPT-5.2 F1 56.8%; complex procedures F1 often below 40%.
links.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 achieved the highest accuracy (F1: 65.9%, precision: 66.7%, recall: 65.2%), followed by Gemini 3 Pro (F1: 62.1%) and GPT-5.2 (F1: 56.8%).

unlisted_practices: Comparing multiple frontier LLMs for medical billing/CPT code assignment against a surgeon-labeled benchmark
Validating LLM-predicted codes against the CMS HCPCS/CPT database to detect hallucinated or invalid codes

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating the accuracy and consistency of frontier LLMs for CPT coding of orthopedic surgical notes against a physician benchmark, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
